samples.summary: Any single 401 anywhere in the app now erases every live offline entry — including non-empty unpushed change logs of documents currently open — from a call site unrelated to the user's intent
samples.evidence: `fetchWithAuth`'s 401 arm (packages/frontend/src/api/auth.ts:250-267) calls `logout({ eraseLocalData: 'keep-archives' })`, which reaches `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout` → `WafflebaseDocStore.dropAllForUser`. `dropAllForUser` (packages/frontend/src/lib/wafflebase-doc-store.ts, `dropAllForUser`) deliberately does NOT spare a document that is open (its own comment says so) and does not spare an entry whose change log is non-empty. Every other deletion path in this same store treats exactly those two conditions as inviolable: `evictOldest` skips any entry with `changeCount > 0` ("a non-empty log is work that may never have reached the server") and `collectStale` skips anything `isLive`. `fetchWithAuth` wraps essentially every request in the app — a notification poll, a sidebar `fetchWorkspaces`, the new `OfflineRuntime` `fetchDocuments()` — so a transient expired cookie or a backend restart, while an editor sits open with unpushed offline work, deletes the durable copy of that work. The inline comment at auth.ts:262-265 justifies it as "copies of content the server holds", which is true of the snapshot but not of the appended change log, which is by construction the un-pushed delta. Fix belongs on the erase call: the 401 path should spare entries with a non-empty log / open documents the way eviction and collection do.

samples.summary: `OfflineRuntime` runs unconditionally for every authenticated session — no `supportsClientKey()` or preference gate — adding an extra `GET /documents` and an IndexedDB database to every signed-in page load on a build where the feature is inert
samples.evidence: `PrivateRoute.tsx:35` mounts `<OfflineRuntime userId={String(me.id)} />` with no gate. `packages/frontend/src/components/offline-runtime.tsx` (effect body, deps `[userId]`) unconditionally constructs a `WafflebaseDocStore` (opening/creating the `wafflebase-offline` database), runs `retryPendingOfflineErase()`, `store.collectStale()`, and `await fetchDocuments()` followed by `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments`. Every other surface of this feature is behind `supportsClientKey()` — `settings/page.tsx` (`offlineAvailable &&`), `sync-status-chip.tsx` (`offerOffline`), `use-durable-document.ts:128` — and the repo is pinned to `@yorkie-js/react@0.7.22` (packages/frontend/package.json:66), i.e. below `MinClientKeyVersion = "0.7.23"`, so nothing can be stored at all on this build. The runtime nonetheless issues one extra `GET /documents` per authenticated session for every user in the product. That request goes through `fetchWithAuth`, so a transient 401 on it triggers the destructive logout path described in the other finding. The fix belongs on the new code: gate `OfflineRuntime`'s work (or its mount) on `supportsClientKey()`.

samples.summary: Every editor mount now fires an extra `GET /auth/me`: the `['me','optional']` query is seeded with `initialData` but no `initialDataUpdatedAt`, so under the default `staleTime: 0` it refetches immediately
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/components/collab-document-provider.tsx:181-188 adds `useQuery({ queryKey: ['me','optional'], queryFn: fetchMeOptional, initialData: () => queryClient.getQueryData<User>(['me']) })` to the one seam every editor passes through (`docs-detail.tsx:351`, `slides-detail.tsx:952`, `document-detail.tsx:910`, `board-detail.tsx:261`, `notes-detail.tsx:378`, `files/pdf-collab.tsx:200`, `shared/shared-document.tsx:1027+`). React Query treats `initialData` without `initialDataUpdatedAt` as `dataUpdatedAt: 0`, which is stale under the default `staleTime`, so `refetchOnMount` fires. On a private route the identity is already resolved under `['me']` (PrivateRoute.tsx:14) and under `['me','optional']` by other components, so opening any document now issues a duplicate `/auth/me`. Passing `initialDataUpdatedAt: () => queryClient.getQueryState(['me'])?.dataUpdatedAt` (or a `staleTime`) would restore the doc-comment's claim that "this costs no extra request".

samples.summary: The design-sandbox `@yorkie-js/react` stub documents an enumerated invariant — "exactly four runtime symbols in use" and "nothing in scope calls `useYorkie()`" — that this change falsifies
samples.evidence: `packages/design-sandbox/src/scenes/canvas/yorkie-offline.tsx:82-87` states that a repo-wide grep of `@yorkie-js/react` imports in `packages/frontend/src` "turns up exactly four runtime symbols in use: `YorkieProvider` (once, in `PrivateRoute.tsx`), `DocumentProvider`, `useDocument`, and `usePresences`", and line 198 says "Nothing in scope calls `useYorkie()`". The diff adds a fifth import site and a fifth symbol: `packages/frontend/src/components/durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:8` imports `useYorkie` and calls it at line 260, and `collab-document-provider.tsx` now also imports `YorkieProvider` — a second `YorkieProvider` use, contradicting "once, in `PrivateRoute.tsx`". Nothing breaks today because the stub re-exports the rest via `export * from "@yorkie-js/react/__wb-real"` (line 124), but the stub's own override list and its `YorkieProvider` pass-through (which drops `clientKey`/`store`) are now maintained against a stale census.

samples.summary: `deleteWorkspace` now issues two extra requests (`GET /workspaces/:ref`, `GET /documents`) before the DELETE for every user, gated on nothing — unlike `removeMember`, which gates its listing on `isOfflineUser`
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/api/workspaces.ts:127 calls `documentIdsIn(id)` unconditionally, which does `fetchWorkspace(ref)` + `fetchDocuments()` (lines 101-115). `removeMember` (line 159-160) guards the same call with `isOfflineUser(String(userId))`; `deleteWorkspace` has no equivalent guard and no `supportsClientKey()`/preference check, so a user who never enabled offline persistence pays two extra round trips on every workspace deletion. The visible fallout is already in the diff: `packages/frontend/src/api/url.test.ts` had to be relaxed from "every request carries the encoded id" to "some request does" specifically because `deleteWorkspace` now makes a companion request. Any other caller or test asserting request count/ordering around workspace deletion is now out of step.

samples.summary: The sync-status design doc still quotes the single-sentence `Not saved` tooltip that this change replaced with two cause-specific branches plus an offer clause
samples.evidence: `docs/design/sync-status.md:147` records the tooltip as *"Changes since <time> haven't reached the server. They exist only in this tab..."*. `packages/frontend/src/components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.tsx` `tooltipFor` now composes it from a connected/disconnected `why` branch, a `risk` sentence, and an optional `offer` clause, and the function signature gained two parameters (`connected`, `offerOffline`). The doc's `saved-locally` additions (lines 50, 442) were updated; this row was not.

samples.summary: A production-source file under `src/lib` imports `vitest` and calls `describe`/`it` at module scope
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/lib/doc-store-contract.ts:1` imports `{ describe, it, expect }` from `"vitest"` (a devDependency) and the exported `testDocStoreContract` calls `describe` directly. It lives outside the suite's `include` globs (`vite.config.ts` `test.include` matches `src/**/*.test.ts`), so it is an ordinary source module that only happens to be imported by `wafflebase-doc-store.test.ts`. Any non-test importer — or a bundler that fails to tree-shake it — pulls a devDependency into the app graph and executes `describe` outside a test context. Naming it `*.contract.test-helper.ts` under a test folder, or moving it beside the suite, keeps it out of the shipped source tree.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repository. fetchWithAuth's 401 arm (packages/frontend/src/api/auth.ts:250-267) calls logout with eraseLocalData:"keep-archives"; logout unconditionally awaits eraseOfflineDataOnLogout (auth.ts:125-127), which reaches WafflebaseDocStore.dropAllForUser via offline-erase.ts:200-232 and :26-32. dropAllForUser (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1031-1075) walks every header key for the user and calls purge() with no isLive check and no changeCount check — its own comment at :1037-1041 states it deliberately does not spare an open document — and purge (:827-835) deletes SNAPSHOTS/HEADERS/CHANGES outright, writing no archive (unlike remove at :757-812, which archives only when expectLoss latched). keepArchives only skips dropArchivesWhere (:1071-1073), so live entries and their unpushed change logs always go. This violates the invariant every other deletion path in the same store upholds: evictOldest skips live entries and any entry with changeCount > 0 (:1361-1362), collectStale skips live entries (:1117-1121), purgeDocument honours skipOpen (:886). Reachability is broad: fetchWithAuth has 85 call sites across 19 api/ and app/ files including background polls (api/notifications.ts, api/workspaces.ts, offline-runtime's fetchDocuments), so a single transient 401 from any of them destroys the durable copy of unpushed offline work for documents currently open. This is an invariant other modules rely on being violated at a call site outside the store — in-lane for blast-radius — and the impact is data loss, i.e. blocking.

verdict.reason: The code is present as described (PrivateRoute.tsx:35 mounts OfflineRuntime ungated; offline-runtime.tsx:59-133 runs the store, sweep and fetchDocuments unconditionally; the pin is 0.7.22 < MinClientKeyVersion 0.7.23), so this is not 'not-present'. It is, however, out of the blast-radius lane's blocking rubric: no caller outside the diff is broken and no guard is bypassed to reach a protected operation. supportsClientKey() is defined and documented as gating the surfaces that OFFER the feature and the code that persists (yorkie-capabilities.ts:70-75; design doc 193-197) — settings/page.tsx:35, sync-status-chip.tsx:146 and collab-document-provider.tsx:196 all still hold unchanged. On this build nothing is stored, so collectStale/purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments delete nothing (offline-erase.ts:338-344 early-returns on an empty accessible list; retryPendingOfflineErase returns before opening IndexedDB at offline-erase.ts:245-249). The once-per-session listing is the documented contract (design doc 266-271), not a violated invariant. The 401-logout escalation adds no new failure mode: PrivateRoute already calls fetchMe through fetchWithAuth on every authenticated load (PrivateRoute.tsx:13-17, api/auth.ts:146-153, 243-270). What remains is one redundant GET and an IDB handle on an inert build — wasted work statable entirely from the new code, minor under this lens, not a major bypass or broken call site.

finding.summary: Eagerly-loaded authenticated shell now statically imports the docs/board/slides/sheets engines, defeating App.tsx's lazy route splitting
finding.evidence: `App.tsx:8` imports `PrivateRoute` statically (every other route is `lazy(...)`, see App.tsx:15-32). `PrivateRoute.tsx:7` now imports `OfflineRuntime` statically, and `offline-runtime.tsx:11` statically imports `@/lib/offline-copy-recovery`, which at `offline-copy-recovery.ts:6,8,9,10` pulls in `@/app/documents/apply-imported-content`, `@/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store`, `@/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store` and `@/app/board/yorkie-board-store`. Those in turn are value-importers of the engine packages: `apply-imported-content.ts:3` (`initialSpreadsheetDocument` from `@wafflebase/sheets`), `:12` (`SYNTHETIC_SLIDE_ID` from `@wafflebase/board`), and `yorkie-board-store.ts:39-40` (`bandBlockNumerics` from `@wafflebase/docs`, `boardToSlidesDocument` from `@wafflebase/board`). The result is that a user who only opens the documents list downloads board/docs/slides/sheets engine code that `vite.config.ts` manualChunks (`sheet-core`, `slides-editor-engine`, `notes-editor-engine`) and the route-level `lazy()` calls exist to keep off that path. The fix belongs on the new code: `recoverOfflineCopy`/`describeArchivedDocument` should be reached through a dynamic `import()` inside the toast action rather than a top-level import.

verdict.reason: The finding's load-bearing claim — that `offline-runtime.tsx:11` statically imports `@/lib/offline-copy-recovery` — is false. Line 11 is `retryPendingOfflineErase,` within the `@/lib/offline-erase` import block (offline-runtime.tsx:8-13), and the module's full top-level import list (lines 1-14) contains no reference to offline-copy-recovery or to any @wafflebase engine package. The recovery module is instead loaded via `await import('@/lib/offline-copy-recovery')` at offline-runtime.tsx:188-190, inside `offerRecoverableWork` and only after `listRecoverableWork` returns a non-empty array (lines 181-182) — i.e. exactly the dynamic-import fix the finding proposes is already in place. A repo-wide grep for `offline-copy-recovery` yields only that dynamic import, the module's own test, and a `vi.mock` in offline-runtime.test.tsx:64; no static importer exists. The remaining eager-shell imports are engine-free: offline-copy.ts:1-2 imports only `@yorkie-js/sdk` plus a type-only store import, and document-list-utils.ts:1-4 imports `date-fns` plus two type-only imports. PrivateRoute.tsx:7,35 does mount OfflineRuntime eagerly, so the shell premise holds, but the engine dependency chain the finding depends on is never formed statically, so the claimed bundle regression does not occur.
